rv.q: David Grindley's acutely staged and acted production of this landmark drama from 1928 is filled with instances of soldiers checking their watches, asking the time, counting off days and hours and minutes.
Seventy-eight years after the Broadway premiere, Sheriff's own lesser-known slice of aching battlefield life turns out to be no less exquisitely humane.
This revival of R.C. Sherriff's 1928. World War I drama is a straightforward, respectful production that honors the material without bringing much fresh insight to bear.
Don’t miss this rare theatrical achievement that may very well be the best revived play of the season.

cn.t: Critics praise this splendid revival of R.C. Sherriff's WWI drama for its persuasive immediacy and haunting power, with David Grindley's acute staging creating a beautifully paced, experiential production that resonates long after.

vs.sum: The Belasco Theatre offers stunning ambiance with its historic Tiffany lamps and stained-glass ceiling, but suffers from tight legroom typical of older venues. While sound quality is generally good, sightlines can be inconsistent, especially from side orchestra seats.

acc.note: 8 wheelchair locations in Orchestra. Induction loops for t-coil hearing aids. Infrared devices available.
